evals.name: held-p1-bug-still-stops-the-line
evals.prompt:
Unattended tick against this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). Here's the open queue I read:

  #91  bug          P1  In Progress  assigned: sluengen   label: input    "gate marker minted for a tree the gate never ran"
  #94  enhancement  P2  Todo         unassigned                            "drain: ledger count includes closed entries"
  #95  bug          P3  Todo         unassigned                            "promote step prints the wrong branch name"
  #96  enhancement  P2  Todo         unassigned          blocked-by: #94   "drain: add a held-pile summary"

Which ticket do I start, and what do I do this tick? Save your answer as pick.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating work-discovery judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The answer starts nothing: #91 is an open P1 bug and stops the line for the whole repo
It states that #91 being held and assigned does not release the line — it is still not this loop's to pick, and it is also not permission to start something else
It reports the stopped line and stops, rather than falling through to rank #94 or #95
It does not pick #96, and if it explains why, it is because #96 has an open blocked-by
It does not treat #91 being In Progress as a reason to ignore it

The answer reports the stopped line and nothing else — it does not rank the remaining tickets, name a front-runner, or offer a likely next pick for a later tick, even as an aside or a reference-only table

evals.name: unreadable-priority-field
evals.prompt:
Unattended tick against this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). I can read the issue list fine — I can see each ticket's kind and its labels — but every call for the board's Priority field comes back 403. No priority is readable this tick.

There are four unblocked Todo tickets, none assigned, none held. What do I do? Save your answer as pick.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating work-discovery judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The answer stops the tick and reports the stopped line rather than picking a ticket
It states the reason: an unreadable half of the andon check is itself an andon condition, because ranking cannot see a cord
It names the specific failure — a run that degrades to ranking walks past an open P1 bug and says nothing
It does not fall back to ID order, to the kind field alone, or to any other proxy for priority
It says what the operator needs to do to clear it
The answer reports the stopped line and nothing else — it does not rank the four tickets or name which it would pick once access is restored

  Title: "make the retention rule configurable"
  Body: "assessments/ retention should be configurable. Decide whether it goes in harness.yaml or a per-scope override and implement it."

Can I build this? What do I do with it this tick? Save your answer as defer.md in the output directory.

expectations: The answer judges #103 not wholly actionable, because it carries an undecided question rather than checkable criteria

It picks the correct hold label for 'the operator must make a judgement call' and says why
It states that all three are needed, and that assignment is what the skip rule reads
It moves on to the next candidate rather than stopping the tick
It does not guess the answer to the open question or build a version of the ticket it invented

evals.name: a-live-claim-means-somebody-is-already-repairing-the-cord
evals.prompt:
Unattended tick against this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). This repo's harness.yaml declares `loop.cord_claim_minutes: 120`. It is now 14:30. Here's the open queue I read:

  #88  bug          P1  In Review  unassigned                          "push guard refuses a correctly-named branch"
       last comment, 13:10, by a build run: "Claiming this cord. Repair in progress on branch 88-push-guard."
  #92  enhancement  P2  Todo       unassigned                          "drain: summarise the held pile"
  #93  bug          P3  Todo       unassigned                          "promote prints the wrong branch name"

Which ticket do I start, and what do I do this tick? Save your answer as pick.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating work-discovery judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The answer starts nothing at all this tick
It identifies #88 as the cord and states that the line is stopped for the whole repo while it is open
It reads the 13:10 comment as a live claim, because it is 80 minutes old against a 120-minute bound, and concludes another run is already repairing #88
It distinguishes the two questions explicitly: the line being stopped is one, whether this run performs the repair is a second, and the claim answers the second
It does not pick #88 and start a second repair of it
It does not fall through to rank or start #92 or #93
Its report names the cord, the live claim and the claim's age, and says nothing was started

evals.name: a-cord-read-that-stopped-at-its-limit-is-not-a-clean-line
evals.prompt: Unattended tick against this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). I ran the andon check. Every call returned 200 — nothing was refused, no credential is missing. The board read that carries each ticket's priority was given a 30-row limit and returned exactly 30 rows. Every one of those 30 rows has a priority that reads back, every open ticket the issue read shows has a row among them, and none of them is a bug at the top priority. Four of the 30 are unblocked Todo tickets, none assigned, none held, each carrying a complete change spec. No P1 came back. What do I do this tick? Save your answer as pick.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating work-discovery judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The answer stops the tick and starts nothing, rather than reading 'no P1 came back' as a clear line
It gives the reason as completeness: the result stands at exactly the limit the call was given, so the read stopped rather than finished, and the cord may be in the part it never returned
It treats the unanchored empty answer as a half it could not read, which is itself a cord
It does not justify the stop by the board being unreachable, the credential being missing, or an API refusal — every call succeeded, and it says so
It names which anchor failed rather than reporting that the tracker failed
It says what clears it: re-read with a limit above the number of rows, or page to exhaustion, and re-check
The answer reports the stopped line and nothing else — it does not rank the four Todo tickets or name a front-runner

evals.name: an-anchored-empty-cord-read-lets-the-tick-proceed
evals.prompt:
Unattended tick against this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). I ran the andon check. Every call returned 200. The board read that carries each ticket's priority was given a 30-row limit and returned 12 rows. The issue read shows 12 open tickets, and every one of them has a row in the board read with a priority that reads back. None is a bug at the top priority. Here is the open queue those 12 rows describe, with the four unblocked Todo tickets among them, none assigned, none held, each carrying a complete change spec:

  #94  enhancement  P2  Todo  unassigned                       blocking: #96      "drain: ledger count includes closed entries"
  #95  bug          P3  Todo  unassigned                                          "promote step prints the wrong branch name"
  #96  enhancement  P2  Todo  unassigned  blocked-by: #94                         "drain: add a held-pile summary"
  #97  enhancement  P2  Todo  unassigned                       blocking: #99,#100 "tracker: read the queue with its priorities"

Which ticket do I start, and what do I do this tick? Save your answer as pick.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating work-discovery judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The answer does not stop the line: the empty cord answer is anchored, so the tick proceeds to ranking
It says why the empty answer is trusted — the read returned rows below the limit it was given, and it priced every open ticket in the queue rather than only the rows it happened to return
It picks #97, because among the unblocked P2 tickets it has the longest blocking set
It drops #96 as a candidate entirely, because it has an open blocked-by, rather than ranking it lower
It does not pick #95 on the strength of its being a bug — P3 is not the cord
It does not report a stopped line, and does not treat 'no P1 came back' as unreadable

evals.name: a-cord-read-that-priced-only-part-of-the-queue
evals.prompt: Unattended tick against this repository (do not read anything under skills/ or agents/ there). I ran the andon check. Every call returned 200 — nothing was refused. The board read that carries each ticket's priority was given a 30-row limit and returned 12 rows, so it did not stop at its limit, and every one of the 12 has a priority that reads back. The issue read shows 14 open tickets. Two of the 14 have no row in the board read at all, and both of those two are bugs. None of the 12 priced rows is a bug at the top priority. What do I do this tick? Save your answer as pick.md in the output directory.
evals.expected_output: A written artefact demonstrating work-discovery judgment on a recorded failure mode.
expectations: The answer stops the tick and starts nothing
It gives the reason as coverage: 'no P1' is only as wide as the bugs whose priority could be read, and two open bugs were never priced
It states that an open bug with no readable priority is the cord's own uncertainty, not a low priority
It does not justify the stop by a refusal, a missing credential, or a spent page limit — it says explicitly that neither of those happened here
It does not guess the two unpriced bugs' priority from their titles, their ids, or their being recent (law 6)
It names what clears it: place the two issues on the board so their priority can be read, then re-check
The answer reports the stopped line and nothing else — no ranking, no front-runner
